item.title: Production Function Estimation With Factor‐Augmenting Technology: An Application to Markups
item.description:
Econometrica ｜ 综合分 67.5 ｜ 上线 2026-11-19（0 天前） · 在线 2026-01-01

I develop a new method for estimating production functions with labor‐augmenting technology and apply it to markup estimation. The method imposes limited parametric restrictions and generalizes prior approaches that rely on the CES production function. I first extend the canonical Olley–Pakes framework assumptions to multidimensional productivity and then develop an identification strategy based on a control variable approach and first‐order conditions. I use this method to estimate output elasticities and markups in manufacturing industries in the US and four developing countries. I find that neglecting labor‐augmenting productivity underestimates capital elasticity, overestimates variable input elasticity, and overestimates markups in all countries.

item.title: Two‐Sided Markets Shaped by Platform‐Guided Search
item.description:
Econometrica ｜ 综合分 49.3 ｜ 上线 2026-11-19（0 天前） · 在线 2026-01-01

This paper investigates concerns that vertically integrated platforms like Amazon steer demand toward their own offers via algorithmic prominence, potentially harming consumers. On Amazon, for each product, the Buybox prominence algorithm selects one seller to feature, influencing which offers consumers consider. Using novel Amazon sales and Buybox (prominence) data, we estimate a structural model capturing the effects of such algorithmic prominence on consumer choices, seller pricing, and entry. We find that the platform can indeed steer demand as 95% of consumers consider only the Buybox offer. The Buybox is highly price‐elastic (−21), but skews toward Amazon's own offers, which are featured as frequently as observably similar offers priced 5% cheaper. Still, as consumers prefer these offers, this skew does not amount to self‐preferencing in the sense of harming consumers: consumer surplus is roughly maximized at the estimated Amazon Buybox advantage, which balances higher prices against showing consumers their preferred offers.

item.title: Intermediate Input Substitutability
item.description:
Econometrica ｜ 综合分 48.5 ｜ 上线 2026-11-19（0 天前） · 在线 2026-01-01

We estimate long‐run elasticities of substitution between intermediate inputs for Indian manufacturing plants. India's trade liberalization in the early 1990s provides an ideal natural policy experiment, with permanent and heterogeneous tariff reductions inducing changes in relative prices which we use for identification. We find a high degree of substitutability at the plant‐level between 8 broad categories of material inputs, significantly above the Cobb–Douglas benchmark of 1. In contrast, when considering shorter time horizons or more transitory shocks to relative prices, we find evidence of much lower elasticities. Using our long‐run elasticities in a quantitative model, we find that misallocation of intermediate inputs causes a reduction in aggregate output of 29%–3.5 times larger relative to a standard calibration with complementary inputs.

item.title: Putting the ‘Finance’ Into ‘Public Finance’: A Theory of Capital Gains Taxation
item.description:
Econometrica ｜ 综合分 46.8 ｜ 上线 2026-11-19（0 天前） · 在线 2026-01-01

Standard optimal capital tax theory abstracts from modeling asset prices, making it unsuitable for thinking about capital gains and wealth taxation. We study optimal redistributive taxation in an environment with asset‐price movements, adopting the modern finance view that asset prices fluctuate not only because of changing cash flows, but also due to other factors (“discount rates”). We show that a combination of realization‐based capital gains and cash flow taxes implements the optimal allocation regardless of the source of asset‐price fluctuations. Moreover, the capital gains tax avoids distortions in portfolio choice (the so‐called lock‐in effect) by targeting total net trades rather than gains from selling individual assets. These results stand in contrast to the classic Haig–Simons comprehensive income tax concept as well as recent proposals for wealth or accrual‐based capital gains taxes.

item.title: From Predictive Algorithms to the Automatic Generation of Anomalies
item.description:
Econometrica ｜ 综合分 45.3 ｜ 上线 2026-11-19（0 天前） · 在线 2026-01-01

How can we extract theoretical insights from machine learning algorithms? We take a familiar lesson: researchers often turn intuition into theoretical insight by constructing “anomalies”—specific examples highlighting hypothesized flaws in a theory, such as the Allais paradox. We develop procedures that replace researchers' intuitions with predictive algorithms: given a predictive algorithm and a theory, our procedures automatically generate anomalies for that theory. We illustrate our procedures by generating anomalies for expected utility theory. Based on a neural network that accurately predicts lottery choices, we recover known anomalies for expected utility theory and discover novel ones. In incentivized experiments, subjects violate expected utility theory on these algorithmically generated anomalies at rates similar to the Allais paradox and common ratio effect.

item.title: Extreme Value Theory With Heterogeneous Agents
item.description:
Econometrica ｜ 综合分 41.0 ｜ 上线 2026-11-19（0 天前） · 在线 2026-01-01

Extreme value processes feature in any economic model in which agents receive a number of draws from some distribution of values and we examine the behavior of the maximum value in the limit as the number of draws becomes large. This paper asks: Do the average outcomes of such processes change when different agents receive a different number of draws? To answer this, we allow the number of draws an agent receives from the underlying distribution of values (e.g., productivities, ideas, or utility shocks) to be given by a search technology , which reflects heterogeneity in the expected number of draws across different types of agents. We derive a new class of extreme value distributions that generalizes the three standard distributions (Fréchet, Gumbel, Weibull) by incorporating heterogeneity across agents. We generalize a result from Gabaix, Laibson, Li, Li, Resnick, and de Vries (2016) regarding extreme value outcomes and consider applications to aggregate productivity, markups, and social networks.

item.title: Optimal Formula Instruments
item.description:
Econometrica ｜ 综合分 41.0 ｜ 上线 2026-11-19（0 天前） · 在线 2026-01-01

When estimating the effects of treatments defined by complex formulas, researchers often use simple functions of exogenous shocks as instruments. A leading example is “simulated instruments” for public policy eligibility, which capture variation in state‐level policy generosity. We show how more powerful instruments can be constructed by incorporating heterogeneous shock exposure while using a recentering procedure to avoid bias. We characterize the asymptotically efficient instruments in this class and propose an algorithm for constructing feasible approximations to them. Compared to a simulated instrument approach, our approach yields a 44% smaller standard error on the private insurance crowd‐out effect of Medicaid enrollment from the 2014 Affordable Care Act expansions.

item.description:

We study a setting in which personal acquisition of information is costly and maintaining personal contacts to share information socially is also costly. The theory predicts star networks, with small groups sustaining an active hub and large groups allowing in addition for an inactive hub equilibrium. Experiments with small (8 subjects) and large (50 subjects) groups show star-like networks throughout. In small groups, behavior matches the active hub prediction. In large groups, hubs are inactive or engage in activity far in excess of the active hub equilibrium depending on how much information subjects are given on their own and others’ earnings. The hub’s activity level shapes relative earnings of subjects and the overall performance of the group. This paper was accepted by Roberto Weber, behavioral economics and decision analysis. item.title: Earnings Instability
item.description:
The Quarterly Journal of Economics ｜ 综合分 39.9 ｜ 上线 2026-11-17（1 天前）

Abstract This paper uses high-frequency administrative data to show that most U.S. workers experience substantial month-to-month fluctuations in pay, even within ongoing employment relationships. Monthly earnings instability is pervasive but is masked in annual data. Moreover, this instability is unequally distributed: lower-income, hourly workers face more instability than higher-income, salaried workers. Firm-driven fluctuations in hours account for a large share of this instability. Monthly earnings instability, in turn, increases spending volatility and job separations. Short-term earnings risk is therefore a significant feature of the labor market and falls disproportionately on the most financially fragile workers.

item.title: Break‐even reference dependence in crop insurance decisions: Theory and evidence
item.description:
American Journal of Agricultural Economics ｜ 综合分 39.3 ｜ 上线 2026-11-17（1 天前）

Abstract We study farmers' crop insurance choices using a behavioral framework in which break‐even status serves as a salient, economically grounded, and empirically observable reference point. The framework nests the standard expected‐utility model as a special case and incorporates three forces: risk reduction, aversion to falling below break‐even status, and disutility from paying premiums. It yields sharp predictions about coverage choices, including bunching at the break‐even coverage level (BECL), defined as the coverage level where the insurance guarantee just covers total cost. We test these predictions using a survey of corn producers in Iowa and Kansas that elicits farmers' perceived BECLs, attitudes toward break‐even protection and premium costs, and their actual Federal Crop Insurance Program coverage choices. Coverage decisions display pronounced and asymmetric bunching around the BECL, with a sharp decline in frequency just below it and a smoother distribution above. Proxy measures of behavioral attitudes are also associated with observed choices in the predicted directions: farmers reporting stronger aversion to not breaking even are more likely to insure exactly at the BECL but not above it, while those reporting stronger premium aversion are more likely to insure below it. Using illustrative simulations, we further examine how subsidy changes interact with these behavioral forces and find that aversion to not breaking even may play an anchoring role that dampens the effects of premium subsidy cuts on coverage choices.

item.title: The Asymmetry in Responsible Investing Preferences and Beliefs
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 37.9 ｜ 上线 2026-11-17（1 天前）

Empirical stylized facts in the literature concerning “sin” versus “angel” stocks display marked asymmetries in investor behavior. Through a set of experiments, we examine whether such biases can be micro-founded via individuals’ preferences and belief formations. With respect to portfolio allocation decisions, we find that the responses to negative environmental and social externalities are several times larger in magnitude than their responses to comparable positive externalities, ceteris paribus. Negative externalities also modestly increase pessimism about future investment performance, whereas positive externalities have little discernible effect on beliefs. This asymmetry is pervasive across our sample, exhibits heterogeneity across individuals, and is comparable to or greater in magnitude than estimates observed in loss aversion analyses. These findings help rationalize several existing stylized empirical facts documented in the responsible investing literature and carry implications for the growing body of theoretical work modeling the role of nonpecuniary investor preferences in asset pricing. This paper was accepted by Marie Claire Villeval, behavioral economics and decision analysis. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.06826 .

item.title: How Do Standard Time Series Forecasting Benchmarks Translate to Finance? A Broad Study of Risk Adjusted Performance
item.description:
Journal of Forecasting ｜ 综合分 35.7 ｜ 上线 2026-11-17（1 天前）

ABSTRACT Forecasting financial asset returns is challenging due to low signal‐to‐noise ratios, nonstationarity and heavy‐tailed distributions. We benchmark 16 deep learning architectures for time series forecasting, including Transformers, State Space Models (SSMs), xLSTMs, and recurrent hybrids, on a 15‐year daily futures dataset using an end‐to‐end volatility‐targeted Sharpe ratio optimization task. Our results challenge prevailing assumptions in the literature. Several widely used “state‐of‐the‐art” architectures, including generic Transformers and SSMs, underperformed a simple AR(1) benchmark in a realistic financial forecasting task. The strongest results came from comparatively simple hybrid approaches using recurrent structures: a Variable Selection Network combined with an LSTM achieved the highest Sharpe ratio, while xLSTM showed the greatest robustness to transaction costs. These findings suggest that success on standard time‐series benchmarks does not reliably transfer to finance, and that architectures tailored to the unique properties of asset returns may remain more effective than generic attention‐based approaches for financial forecasting.

item.title: Does Feedback Enhance Diversity in Selection Decisions?
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 35.1 ｜ 上线 2026-11-17（1 天前）

Some organizations provide employees with feedback on the demographics of people they have chosen to spotlight, hire, and promote, hoping to spur more diverse future selections. However, it is an open question whether purely descriptive feedback accomplishes this. We theorize and show that descriptive feedback highlighting low past selection rates of women or racial minorities (e.g., “5% of previous experts interviewed were women”) triggers a motivation to respond without prejudice, increasing the subsequent selection of members of underrepresented groups. Conversely, providing descriptive feedback about low selection rates of people with other attributes (e.g., areas of expertise, geographical location) that do not evoke image or reputational concerns has less influence on future decisions. We demonstrate these patterns across seven preregistered experiments (total n = 6,502), including one framed field experiment (Study 2). One study identifies motivation to respond without prejudice as a mediator of the effect of descriptive feedback about past choices on future selections of women and racial minorities. Another study shows that when women are overrepresented, the effect of descriptive feedback reverses in direction, increasing the subsequent selection of men (due to concerns about fairness), but this effect is significantly smaller in magnitude than the feedback effect produced when women are underrepresented. Practically, the effects of descriptive feedback were 45%–80% as large as simulating a strict quota requiring that at least one woman or racial minority be selected for a given opportunity, highlighting that descriptive feedback is a light-touch but potentially powerful intervention for promoting diversity. This paper was accepted by George Wu, behavioral economics and decision analysis. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.01479 .

item.title: Human Performance at Solving 0-1 Knapsack Problems: Results from a Large-Scale Field Experiment
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 35.1 ｜ 上线 2026-11-17（1 天前）

The 0-1 knapsack problem is a fundamental problem of discrete choice that permeates many diverse fields and applications, but relatively little is known about what instances human solvers find more difficult than others. This paper reports the results of the first large-scale randomized controlled field experiment investigating this question, conducted in partnership with a global mobile gaming platform. A total of 100,000 different knapsack instances were predesigned for this study and randomly assigned to each player attempt at the knapsack problem. For our base-case analysis, there were 17,950,838 distinct player accounts who made a total of 150,284,195 submitted solution attempts. Contrary to expectations, players performed better on problems that were rated as more difficult by two traditional measures of knapsack difficulty (the Pearson correlation between value and weight vectors and Sahni complexity), but performed worse on problem instances that featured large optimality gaps from a suite of heuristic solution algorithms. These suggest that optimality gaps can serve as promising measures of human-perceived knapsack difficulty and potentially could be used to measure human-perceived problem difficulty for other types of discrete choice problems. We found evidence that players improved their performance with repeated attempts at the knapsack task overall, but less-experienced players of the mobile game improved more quickly than more-experienced players. Through the construction of a new measure of human-perceived difficulty rating for each knapsack instance, we found evidence that players who were assigned to instances with a higher difficulty rating in the past tended to perform better on future attempts. item.title: A Credit Risk Assessment Model Based on SVM With a Hypersphere‐Based Adaptive Oversampling Technique
item.description:
Journal of Forecasting ｜ 综合分 29.6 ｜ 上线 2026-11-17（0 天前） · 在线 2026-11-16

ABSTRACT Credit risk prediction for small and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs) is challenging under imbalanced data conditions, where the scarcity of high‐risk SME samples undermines the performance of traditional classifiers. However, SME credit risk studies addressing data imbalance have mainly focused on class imbalance, while other performance‐degrading data difficulty factors, such as outliers, small disjuncts, and class overlap, remain underexplored. To address these challenges, we develop a customized credit risk assessment framework, termed DCHO‐SVM, that integrates the DCHO oversampling method for data preprocessing with SVM for classification. The model first employs principal component analysis (PCA) to reduce data dimensionality and derives a compact feature representation from the constructed indicator system. Subsequently, DCHO preprocesses the training data by dynamically constructing hyperspheres, adaptively determining their oversampling weights based on local distribution characteristics to address within‐class imbalance, and then performing oversampling within the hyperspheres to avoid class overlap. Finally, the balanced training set obtained after oversampling is used to train the SVM classifier, which is subsequently utilized for SME credit risk prediction. Empirical analysis on 551 Chinese listed manufacturing SMEs shows that the proposed model outperforms the conventional classifier, with , , , , and improving from 0.741, 0.507, 0.763, 0.602, and 0.455 to 0.924, 0.752, 0.935, 0.920, and 0.734, respectively. In addition, robustness tests on various real‐world imbalanced credit datasets from UCI and Fannie Mae repositories further verify the effectiveness and generalizability of the proposed model. These results indicate that DCHO‐SVM provides an effective solution for SME credit risk assessment under complex imbalanced scenarios.

item.title: Biodiversity Risk in the Corporate Bond Market
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 41.1 ｜ 上线 2026-11-16（1 天前）

We show that a biodiversity risk premium has emerged in the U.S. corporate bond market following the United Nations Biodiversity Conference (COP15) in October 2021. COP15 placed biodiversity on the global regulatory agenda and raised transition risks for exposed firms. After COP15, a one standard deviation increase in a firm’s biodiversity footprint is associated with a 7% increase in its secondary market yield spreads, whereas this relation is insignificant before COP15. The biodiversity effect is also present in primary bond markets, most pronounced for medium-term bonds and distinct from climate-related mechanisms. Furthermore, a higher biodiversity footprint is associated with a lower likelihood of issuing medium-term bonds after COP15, consistent with firms managing their biodiversity-related risks. Evidence from firms’ biodiversity dependencies suggests that physical biodiversity risks are also priced in the bond market. This paper was accepted by Bo Becker, finance. item.title: Whiplash: Congestion Dissipation in a Disrupted Circulatory Shipping System
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 40.4 ｜ 上线 2026-11-16（1 天前）

The (post)pandemic period was marked by numerous port disruptions, leading to delays and rising costs for shippers. We build a fluid model in transient states to investigate how a disruption at one port can affect the disrupted port and its counterpart in another country in a circulatory container shipping system, where a stream of fleets moves goods back and forth between the two ports. Port disruption leads to two types of congestion: the inbound backlogs, which occur when ships are unable to enter the port, and the outbound backlogs, which arise when goods are unable to be loaded onto ships for transport to other ports. We analytically characterize the system’s recovery time, measured from the onset of the port closure until normal operations are restored, and the dynamics of inbound and outbound backlogs during recovery. We identify a whiplash effect in which outbound backlogs alternate between ports, creating oscillatory congestion patterns because of the disruption-induced uneven spatial distribution of ships. Our analysis reveals that simply increasing ship capacity may not expedite system recovery, highlighting the importance of coordination between port authorities and shipping companies when jointly planning capacity expansions. Furthermore, we examine several extensions of the model. We use the two-port system as a building block to analyze bipartite and cyclic network structures, and we also consider scenarios in which a port experiences multiple disruptions. In all cases, the whiplash effect persists, thereby demonstrating the robustness of our findings. Finally, we use our theory model prediction as a feature and apply machine learning techniques to predict the time that vessels spend in Shanghai Port after a typhoon disruption and show that using our model predictor, alongside all relevant vessel and voyage attributes as raw features, significantly reduces prediction errors by 10%–30% on average compared with not using it. This paper was accepted by Elena Katok, operations management. Funding: This work was supported by the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada [Grant RGPIN-2021-04295]. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.05427 .

item.title: Do Fund Managers’ Commitments to Responsible Investing Affect Private Information Acquisition, Information Environment, and Corporate Sustainability?
item.description:

We investigate the effects of mutual funds’ commitments to responsible investing on their information acquisition activities and the corresponding externalities for other stakeholders. After committing to responsible investing (via United Nations Principles for Responsible Investment (UNPRI)), fund managers increase private information acquisition activities, that is, corporate site visits, particularly focusing on environmental and social issues. These visits generate negligible private investment value for the visiting funds. In addition to the information production role of these visits, they also generate positive externalities for other stakeholders through incremental improvements in the sustainability practices of the firms receiving sustainability-focused site visits from UNPRI fund managers. item.title: Advertising by Recruiting Influencers
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 32.9 ｜ 上线 2026-11-16（1 天前）

The rise of social media platforms has enabled customers to rely on influencers and peer reviews to guide their purchasing decisions. As products increasingly focus on experiences, firms are leveraging influencer marketing as a crucial tool. This paper addresses key challenges of influencer marketing by considering different types of influencers and partnership schemes alongside the impact of social learning. We introduce a two-period model wherein, in the initial period, the firm unveils a new product experience of unknown quality alongside an influencer marketing campaign. The campaign relies on two types of influencers that differ in popularity and engagement levels and two partnerships: sponsored advertising and public relations. Customers base their purchasing decisions on their original (heterogeneous) beliefs, influencer-driven information, and reviews from early adopters in the second period. When customers are equally likely to follow any given influencer, the firm should choose a single influencer type and partnership. Consumer reviews complement influencer marketing when products are initially undervalued, increasing the returns to influencer investment. Moreover, within a societal structure characterized by distinct classes, in which followers and influencers often belong to the same class, a mix of influencer types and partnership schemes may become optimal. Our study provides guidance on selecting influencer types, partnership schemes, and social media platforms based on engagement, popularity, audience composition, and platform characteristics. This paper was accepted by Jeanette Song, operations management. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.07919 .

item.title: Hybrid Forecasting Model for Carbon Price: Integrating Chronological and Weekday‐Structured Temporal Representations
item.description:
Journal of Forecasting ｜ 综合分 74.3 ｜ 上线 2026-11-14（1 天前） · 在线 2026-11-13

ABSTRACT Accurate carbon price forecasts support allowance trading, compliance planning and market supervision. This study examines whether two temporal representations of the same carbon price series—the original chronological sequence (horizontal dimension) and five weekday‐structured subsequences (vertical dimension) obtained by regrouping Monday‐to‐Friday observations—contain complementary predictive information. Both representations are modeled within a common decomposition‐reconstruction‐forecasting framework: Dynamic time warping (DTW) diagnoses the correspondence between them, complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) and sample entropy (SE) decompose and reconstruct each series, and a leaky‐integrator echo state network (LiESN) generates the forecasts. The weekday‐specific forecasts are restored to chronological order and fused with the horizontal forecast by least squares (LS), and kernel density estimation (KDE) is used to construct prediction intervals. In the Hubei carbon market, the proposed model achieves an MAE of 0.365, a MAPE of 0.800%, an RMSE of 0.538 and an R 2 of 0.949 in the test period, reducing the MAE, MAPE, and RMSE of the chronological‐only benchmark by 2.41%, 2.20%, and 2.89%, respectively, and the Wilcoxon signed‐rank test indicates that its improvements over all benchmark models are significant at the 5% level. The model also attains the highest or tied‐highest interval coverage and the highest composite interval score. Additional experiments on the Shenzhen and Chongqing carbon markets show that the incremental gain is modest, and its statistical significance is market‐dependent: It is significant in Chongqing but not in Shenzhen. These results support the view that weekday‐structured forecasts can provide complementary predictive information beyond adjacent‐day chronological dependence, without treating the weekday sequences as independent multivariate variables or claiming a newly discovered weekday anomaly.

item.title: The Economics of Waste Valorization
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 35.8 ｜ 上线 2026-11-13（1 天前）

As the spread of waste imposes substantial environmental and economic burdens, a newer operational strategy, waste valorization, is gaining attention. This approach transforms production-generated byproduct waste into valuable, distinct products, creating intricate production and demand interdependencies that traditional strategies like remanufacturing and coproduction cannot fully capture. In this study, we examine the impacts of these interdependencies within a two-stage stochastic production decision model to determine optimal production quantities under waste valorization. When product demands are uncorrelated, the manufacturer’s optimal profit can exhibit an inverse U-shaped relationship with the valorization rate, attaining its maximum at a moderate level that maintains a perfect balance in production. Conversely, when product demands are correlated, the manufacturer employs a “pool-to-center” strategy, using different pooling policies to smooth production quantities and minimize disparities with respect to the valorization rate. Surprisingly, as demand randomness or correlation intensifies, the optimal profit becomes M-shaped, with profit maximum shifting toward either low or high valorization rates, a phenomenon we term “go-to-extreme.” Although waste valorization can yield both economic and environmental benefits, we caution that a more efficient waste valorization process may lead to negative outcomes for both the manufacturer and the environment. This analysis not only sheds light on how waste valorization contributes to waste reduction and economic value, but also provides insights for production decision making. item.description:

We study a censored variant of the data-driven newsvendor problem, where the decision maker must select an ordering quantity that minimizes expected overage and underage costs based only on offline censored sales data rather than historical demand realizations. This set is defined by the largest historical order quantity (the observable boundary of the data set), and contains all distributions matching the true demand distribution up to this boundary while allowing them to be arbitrary afterward. We demonstrate a spectrum of achievability under demand censoring by deriving a natural necessary and sufficient condition under which vanishing regret is an achievable goal. In regimes in which it is not, we exactly characterize the information loss due to censoring: an insurmountable lower bound on the performance of any policy, even when the decision maker has access to infinitely many demand samples. We then leverage these sharp characterizations to propose a natural robust algorithm that adapts to the historical level of demand censoring. We derive finite-sample guarantees for this algorithm across all possible censoring regimes and show its near-optimality with matching lower bounds (up to polylogarithmic factors). We moreover demonstrate its robust performance via extensive numerical experiments on both synthetic and real-world data sets. This paper was accepted by Wolfram Wiesemann, data science. item.title: Effortful vs. Opportunistic Consumption of Discretionary Time: How Time-Reporting Decisions Influence Extra-Role Effort
item.description:
Management Science ｜ 综合分 37.9 ｜ 上线 2026-11-12（1 天前）

Employees often work under incomplete contracts, performing both contracted in-role tasks and valuable but noncontracted extra-role activities. Once employees have completed in-role tasks, discretionary time remains, which they may allocate to extra-role activities or consume opportunistically. This study examines how managers’ time-reporting decisions, as a less intrusive form of control, affect subordinates’ effort-allocation decisions. I propose two opposing predictions. First, managers’ control implementations may signal distrust, resulting in more opportunism and thus less extra-role effort. Second, I identify value signaling as a novel theoretical mechanism through which time-reporting decisions may increase extra-role effort. The main experiment manipulated two factors: the type of time report (aggregated versus disaggregated) and its implementation source (managerial choice versus random assignment) to isolate signaling effects from monitoring effects. Results reveal that when managers choose not to implement disaggregated time reporting—that is, reports that make discretionary time salient—subordinates significantly reduce their extra-role effort. Structural equation modeling shows that value signaling outweighs distrust signaling in driving employees’ effort-allocation decisions. In contrast, when the time-reporting format is randomly assigned, effort remains unchanged, underscoring the signaling role of managerial choice. An additional online experiment shows directionally consistent results with the main experiment. These findings reveal a hidden cost of not controlling and contribute to the literature on incomplete contracts, slack resources, and input-based controls in modern work contexts. Abstract Germany experienced a sharp rise in wage inequality over the two decades leading up to the Great Recession. Abstract In order to quantify the impact of agricultural policy uncertainty on European farmers' investment behavior, we construct a newspaper‐based monthly index of European agricultural policy uncertainty from 2013 to 2023. item.title: Inequality and Racial Backlash: Evidence from the Reconstruction Era and the Freedmen's Bureau
item.description:
American Economic Review ｜ 综合分 37.4 ｜ 上线 2026-10-30（1 天前） · 期号 2026-11

How do majority groups respond to narrowing inequality in racially polarized environments? We study this by examining the Freedmen's Bureau, an agency created after the US Civil War to aid former slaves and launch institutional reform in the South. Using new historical records and an event-study approach, we estimate the bureau's impact on political, social, and economic outcomes. Vote shares for Democrats, the party that previously championed slavery and opposed Black civil rights, initially eroded in bureau counties, but these impacts faded as federal oversight weakened. Racial backlash emerged rapidly and persisted, suggesting White majorities sought to offset Black progress. (JEL D63, D72, J15, N31, N41)

item.title: The Effects of School Phone Bans: National Evidence from Lockable Pouches
item.description:
The Quarterly Journal of Economics ｜ 综合分 37.4 ｜ 上线 2026-10-30（1 天前）

Abstract Schools across the U.S. have sharply restricted student use of phones during the school day. We evaluate one type of restriction—lockable phone pouches—using nationwide data combining a large-scale teacher survey, GPS pings, standardized test scores, and school administrative records, along with sales records from the largest pouch provider. Using a staggered difference-in-differences design, we find that pouch adoption substantially reduces phone use as measured by GPS pings and teacher reports. In the first year after adoption, disciplinary incidents increase, and we find suggestive evidence that student subjective well-being falls, consistent with short-term disruption. However, disciplinary effects fade, while the estimated effects on well-being appear to recover and become positive in later years. For academic achievement, average effects on test scores are consistently close to zero. High schools see modest positive effects, particularly in math, while middle schools see small negative effects. We find little evidence of effects on school attendance and no clear evidence of improvements in self-reported classroom attention or perceived online bullying.

Based on a narrative classification of all significant postwar changes in R&D appropriations for five major federal agencies, we find that an increase in nondefense R&D appropriations leads to increases in various measures of innovative activity and higher business-sector productivity in the long run. We structurally estimate the production function elasticity of nondefense government R&D capital using the SP-IV methodology of Lewis and Mertens (2024) and obtain implied returns of 140 to 210 percent over the postwar period. The estimates indicate that government-funded R&D accounts for one-fifth of business-sector TFP growth since WWII and imply substantial underfunding of nondefense R&D. item.description:
American Economic Review ｜ 综合分 37.1 ｜ 上线 2026-10-30（1 天前） · 期号 2026-11

This paper considers how far private adaptation may reduce future vulnerability to climate risks. Using data on monthly firm-to-firm transactions from Pakistan, we find that flood-affected firms are more likely to relocate to safer ground and shift purchases toward suppliers in less flood-prone regions and reached via less flood-prone roads. The results indicate that firms are imperfectly informed about flood risk and update their beliefs following floods. We quantify aggregate impacts using a spatial model of endogenous production network formation. The findings suggest that firms' learning will shape the economic impact of increasingly frequent climate-related disasters. (JEL D22, L14, O13, O14, Q54, R32)

ABSTRACT We consider an informed large shareholder who can choose between making a takeover bid herself and initiating a sale to another acquirer. Such takeover activism complements direct takeovers because the very choice mitigates the asymmetric information problem, thereby improving efficiency. As more investors enter the market for corporate control, takeover activism increasingly replaces direct takeovers as the prevailing mode of disciplinary control change, matching the evolution in practice. Our model shows how this evolution, characterized by a symbiotic relationship between investor activism and private equity, arises to overcome asymmetric information and collective action problems through intermediated transactions.
